newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters repeats defence of Morgan at news briefing.
newsitem.headline: Peters repeats defence of Morgan at news briefing.

text.p: New Zealand's Deputy Prime Minister and New Zealand First Leader Winston Peters used a news conference on Thursday to repeat his defence of NZ First MP Tukuroirangi Morgan against claims of mispending.

He told reporters that the latest reports in The Dominion newspaper were baseless. Earlier he had told Radio New Zealand he did not believe Morgan would be resigning over the allegations linked to his connections with Aotearoa Television Network (ATN).
"I will not stand by and watch a colleague of mine being maltreated without any evidence," Peters told reporters.
Asked if he expected an ongoing investigation by the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) into Morgan and ATN to clear his fellow MP, Peters said, "I don't know, but I am happy to wait."
Officials have made plain that the government continues to be concerned about the extensive media coverage of a range of spending allegations about Morgan.
However, Prime Minister Jim Bolger's office was quoted as saying on radio today that he would not be commenting until the SFO had completed its report.
Asked it he had confidence in everything that Morgan had told him he said when someone tells you somthing is true you have to have confidence in their word.
Asked if Prime Minister Jim Bolger was aware of all the details he said, "he has known the details as I have known".
Peters acknowledged the furore had been damaging.
"I have got no doubt what the public perception is. It is hurting me, it is hurting my party, it is hurting the coalition."
